manifest.purpose: Correct analysis report matching schema in interface: top-level findings (array), overall_assessment (string), is_trojan_present (boolean, true). Findings must contain one primary high-confidence (>=0.9) entry naming the hidden rare-trigger counter/comparator signal 'trig_cnt' (or exact identifier as it appears in inputs/aes_core.v) with activation_condition describing trig_cnt reaching rare 16-bit constant 16'hBEEF AND round-state register (e.g. state_reg/round_cnt equals specific value) simultaneously, affected_outputs=['out_data'] only (must be a real declared output port of aes_core module). Description must state payload XORs exactly one bit of out_data for one cycle. May include a secondary lower-confidence finding referencing the payload mux/XOR gate net feeding out_data, distinct signal_name from the comparator, still only referencing real identifiers from aes_core.v and real output ports in affected_outputs. Must NOT list documented legitimate signals (round_cnt, state_reg used for normal AES rounds) as high-confidence (>=0.5) spurious findings — at most one such mention with confidence <0.5 if needed for context, to keep false_positive_rate low and avoid triggering SR4/egregious-flooding fail condition. overall_assessment: concise text summarizing rare-trigger/payload-mux trojan found, is_trojan_present: true. All signal_name and affected_outputs values must exactly match verbatim identifiers/ports declared in inputs/aes_core.v so FR3/FR4 pass; this file is graded standalone by evaluate.py against inputs/aes_core.v and hidden_spec ground truth, no other files are read.
